summary: Reverse a list of characters in place.
mainInsight: Swap the mirrored elements s[l] and s[r] while moving the pointers toward each other; each pair is swapped once so it is O(n) time, O(1) space.

promptVariants: Which technique reverses an array in place?
What pattern pairs the first and last elements?
options: Two pointers moving inward from both array ends
Sliding window over the array from the left
Binary search for the swap positions in the array
A stack that pops the elements back in reverse
cards.answer: Two pointers moving inward from both array ends
cards.explanation: Mirrored indices are swapped until the pointers meet.

promptVariants: Reversing a character list with two pointers takes ___ time.
Extra space of the two-pointer solution: ___
In-place Reverse String uses ___ extra space.
Does `while l <= r` vs `while l < r` matter here?
What happens when l == r in your loop?
cards.code:
l, r = 0, len(s) - 1
while l <= r:
    s[l], s[r] = s[r], s[l]
    l += 1
    r -= 1
cards.answer: When l == r the swap is a harmless self-swap of the middle element; `l < r` skips it. Both are correct; `l < r` avoids one redundant operation.

promptVariants: What does the algorithm do for a single character?
How many swaps happen for odd length n?
options: No real swap; the single middle element stays put
It raises an error since there is no pair to swap
It deletes the character from the array entirely
It needs special casing before the loop starts
cards.answer: No real swap; the single middle element stays put
cards.explanation: The pointers coincide immediately, so at most a self-swap occurs.
